title: Take-Two 传唤微软和 Discord，试图阻止《Grand Theft Auto VI》大规模泄露

Take-Two subpoenas Microsoft, Discord in bid to halt Grand Theft Auto VI leak
Business
Console
News
Take-Two subpoenas Microsoft and Discord in bid to halt extensive Grand Theft Auto VI leak
Take-Two is racing to halt a series of GTA VI leaks from an entity known as "Cyberleek" that may have access to a playable build of the game.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
August 21, 2026
3 Min Read
Image via Take-Two Interactive/Rockstar Games
Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive is taking legal action to track down the individual or individuals known as "Cyberleek" that has spent the week leaking footage from what appears to be an older build of the upcoming game
Grand Theft Auto VI
.
According to Kotaku
, Take-Two has subpoenaed software conglomerate Microsoft and communications chat platform Discord to track down information about the unknown leaker.
Take-Two is making separate requests for each of the two companies as it seeks to halt the release of any further leaks, asking each company to comply by September 4. Of Microsoft, it is petitioning the company to produce "all internal Microsoft business records and investigative records associated with Microsoft's internal investigation of the 'cyberleek' persona sufficient to identify the user(s), person(s) and/or entity/ies associated with that persona."
The petition apparently makes reference to a Github repository where leaked content had been posted (Microsoft
purchased Github
in 2018). It's also looking for any identifying information about users interacting with specific Discord servers and access to any affiliated individuals' OneDrive account.

Discord has been asked to provide records of specific Discord users and servers. One such server is affiliated with content creator Matthew Judge, who
posted on X
that he was unclear why his server had been identified in the subpoena.
"I don't know anything. That isn't my editors discord. There aren't even any clips of the leaks in either of my Discords," Judge wrote. He speculated that his server might have been swept up because of possible references to his content in some videos released by Cyberleek.
The
GTA VI
leaker has threatened to target other large game publishers
It's not surprising that Take-Two might be casting such a wide net—especially
when according to Bloomberg News
, the company currently has no information regarding Cyberleek's identity or any explanation for how it gained access to such confidential material.
The company is reportedly not allowing these events to alter its upcoming major trailer reveal for the game that will be released
in partnership with Netflix
.
Sources speaking to Bloomberg also described the mood of employees and company leaders as "angry." This is
the second time
Rockstar has been targeted in a major cybersecurity breach, and the company implemented strict security policies following the first incident. Bloomberg reports that this included a full return-to-office mandate for hybrid and remote workers, and that some workers are frustrated that a second hack has taken place even following the reportedly controversial changes.
Related:
Makers Fund expands game industry footprint through $250 million investment round
Developers and industry professionals not employed by Rockstar should be aware that Cyberleek has posted a wider threat targeting video game publishers who fail to abide by its "commandments." These commandments come from a manifesto posted on its website (reviewed by Game Developer). These commandments concern digital pre-orders, day-one downloadable content (DLC), and online game preservation.
It concludes with a warning to "all big corpo" that they might become the next target.
Game Developer has reached out to Take-Two Interactive for comment on this story and will update it upon the company's response.
